name: ADG884BRMZ
title: 0.5 Ω CMOS dual 2:1 multiplexer / SPDT audio switch
summary: The ADG884 holds two SPDT CMOS switches, each steered by its own logic input, for a 1.8 V to 5.5 V single supply. On resistance is 0.28 Ω typical at VDD = 4.5 V, flat within 0.1 Ω typical across a rail-to-rail signal, and each switch carries 400 mA continuous. It comes in a 10-lead MSOP, a 3 mm × 3 mm LFCSP and a 2 mm × 1.5 mm WLCSP.

circuits.title: Switching-time test circuit (tON, tOFF)
circuits.description: Switch 1 carries a DC level VS from S1B to D1, with S1A grounded. D1 drives a 50 Ω load in parallel with 35 pF. A pulse on IN1 flips the switch; tON and tOFF run from the 50% point of the logic edge to the 90% point of the output. VDD is decoupled by 0.1 µF.

circuits.title: Break-before-make test circuit (tBBM)
circuits.description: Both throws of switch 1 are tied to the same level VS, so the output on D1 dips only while neither throw is connected. tBBM is the gap between the 80% points of the output as the switch leaves one throw and reaches the other. Load is 50 Ω with 35 pF; VDD is decoupled by 0.1 µF.

circuits.title: Charge-injection test circuit
circuits.description: VS drives D1; S1A feeds a 1 nF capacitor whose voltage is the output, and S1B is left open. When IN1 switches S1A off, the step ΔVOUT left on the capacitor gives the injected charge as QINJ = CL × ΔVOUT.

circuits.title: Off-isolation test circuit
circuits.description: A network analyzer's 50 Ω source drives S1A, which is also terminated by 50 Ω to ground, while the switch is set to S1B (left open). D1 goes to the analyzer's 50 Ω input. Off isolation is 20 log(VOUT/VS). The links to the analyzer are coaxial with grounded shields; VDD is decoupled by 0.1 µF.
notes: IN1 selects S1B.

circuits.title: Insertion-loss and bandwidth test circuit
circuits.description: The analyzer's 50 Ω source drives S1A, the switch is closed onto S1A, and D1 goes to the analyzer's 50 Ω input; S1B is grounded. Insertion loss is 20 log of VOUT with the switch over VOUT without it; the −3 dB bandwidth comes from the same sweep. Coaxial links with grounded shields; VDD decoupled by 0.1 µF.
notes: The captions of Figures 25 and 26 are swapped: this is the insertion-loss and bandwidth circuit (Figure 26).
IN1 selects S1A.

circuits.title: Crosstalk test circuit, S1A to S1B
circuits.description: The analyzer's 50 Ω source drives S1B, which is selected onto D1, and D1 is loaded by 50 Ω. The unselected S1A goes to the analyzer's 50 Ω input. Crosstalk is 20 log(VOUT/VS). Coaxial links with grounded shields; VDD decoupled by 0.1 µF.
notes: The captions of Figures 25 and 26 are swapped: this is the S1A−S1B crosstalk circuit (Figure 25).
IN1 selects S1B.

circuits.title: Crosstalk test circuit, S1A to S2A
circuits.description: The analyzer's 50 Ω source drives S1A, selected onto D1, which is loaded by 50 Ω; S1B is open. On switch 2, S2A is selected and goes to the analyzer's 50 Ω input, while D2 and S2B are tied together and left open. Crosstalk between the two switches is 20 log(VOUT/VS).
notes: No connection is given for VDD, GND, IN1 or IN2.

where.V1: voltage measured across the closed switch from S to D

where.CL: load capacitor on the output, 1 nF
where.ΔVOUT: step in output voltage when the switch turns off

where.VOUT: level coupled onto the unselected path

equations.name: Insertion loss
equations.expr: Insertion loss = 20 log(VOUT with switch / VOUT without switch)

operation.text: Two single-pole double-throw switches, each with its own logic input. A high on IN1 (IN2) connects D1 (D2) to S1A (S2A); a low connects it to S1B (S2B). Each switch opens the old path before closing the new one (break-before-make, 10 ns minimum).
A closed switch passes current equally in either direction, and the signal may swing from GND to VDD.

Runs from a single 1.8 V to 5.5 V supply. The logic inputs are 1.8 V logic compatible; VINH is 2.0 V minimum at VDD = 5 V ± 10% and 3.4 V to 4.2 V, and 1.3 V minimum at VDD = 2.7 V to 3.6 V; VINL is 0.8 V maximum. Supply current is 0.003 µA typical, 1 µA maximum, with the logic inputs at 0 V or VDD.
Each S or D terminal carries 400 mA continuous and 600 mA peak (1 ms pulses, 10% duty cycle at most) at a 5 V supply; 400 mA continuous is also given for a 3.3 V supply.
On resistance stays under 0.4 Ω over temperature at VDD = 4.5 V (0.28 Ω typical, 0.38 Ω maximum at 100 mA), rising to 0.6 Ω maximum at 2.7 V; flatness is 0.15 Ω maximum at 4.5 V.
THD + N into 32 Ω over 20 Hz to 20 kHz is 0.01% typical at VDD = 4.2 V with 2 V p-p, 0.017% at 5 V with 3.5 V p-p and 0.03% at 2.7 V to 3.6 V with 1.5 V p-p.
IN, S and D have clamp diodes to the rails. Beyond the supplies the current into these pins must be held to the absolute maximum ratings: the digital inputs to 10 mA.
The part is sensitive to electrostatic discharge and needs ESD handling precautions.
